name: Danaher Pin Escape Fundamentals System
description: Find a route through John Danaher's Pin Escapes & Turtle Escapes course by matching the pin, escape family and resulting position.
summary: John Danaher's Pin Escapes & Turtle Escapes connects general escape concepts with mount, side-pin, north-south, rear-mount and turtle material.
overview: The outline devotes several volumes to side-position escapes rather than treating all pins as one problem. A useful way into this long course is to identify both the starting pin and the destination you want to understand, then compare variants within that section.

products.title: Pin Escapes & Turtle Escapes: BJJ Fundamentals - Go Further Faster
products.blurb: An eight-volume positional escape course, with extensive mount and side-pin sections plus rear mount and turtle.
products.best_for: Students building a map of bottom-position escapes or comparing variants from a recurring pin.
products.study_focus: Start at Volume 1, Escapes Overview (6:56); then use the mount families in Volume 2 or the side-position sections in Volumes 3–6.

guide.display_title: John Danaher: Pin Escapes and Turtle Escapes

fits: You need an organized introduction to recovery from several bottom positions.
You want to compare mount or side-pin escape families before choosing one lesson to study closely.
consider_alternative_if: Established rear mount is your main problem: Back Defense Protocol offers Glick's more finely divided overhook-side, underhook-side and body-triangle outline.

includes: Volume 1 covers escape goals, pinning concepts and body movements; Volumes 2–3 develop mount bridging and elbow-escape material.
Volumes 3–6 address side-position elbow and knee escapes, framing, insertion points and several alternative escape families.
Volume 7 includes knee-on-belly and north-south; Volume 8 covers rear mount and turtle.
limits: The organizing subject is positional escape; a specific submission already in progress may call for a separate submission-defense lesson.
The outline names minimal and positive escapes but does not define those categories in its public text.

start_here.title: Compare the starting pin with the destination
start_here.task: Choose one mount or side-control exchange and describe its first and last recognizable positions. Did it end in guard, standing, another pin or an unclear scramble? For mount, locate the bridge and elbow-escape families in Volume 2; for side control, compare the elbow material beginning in Volume 3 with the knee-escape material in Volume 4. Begin course viewing with Escapes Overview to check how Danaher defines the outcome you are trying to study.
start_here.section: Volume 1: Escapes Overview (6:56–43:37); Volume 2: Bridging Escape From Mounted Position (UPA) (0:00) and Elbow Escape From Mounted Position (30:01)
